knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# What this notebook does

Five reporter constructs are scored by the models built on MDA-MB-231 transcripts, to ask how
much each one *looks like* an mRNA whose translation depends on eIF3d:

* the **NanoLuc synonymous series** - a parent, a codon-**adapted** variant, an
  **anti-adapted** variant, and a **negative control** that is a positional shuffle of the
  parent's own codons. These four share one backbone, one protein and one CDS length, so only
  codon choice separates them.
* **firefly** (luc2P), the transfection-efficiency normaliser the assays divide by. It is
  **not** a member of that series - different vector UTRs, a non-human ORF, 2.8x the CDS
  length - and it is here for a different question: a normaliser that is itself
  eIF3d-dependent would subtract part of the effect being measured.

**Read the two questions separately.** Within the synonymous series the comparison is
controlled and the separation is close to arithmetic, since codon usage is what the strongest
features measure. Firefly's score is a *screen*, not a controlled contrast.

**Every number here is a median over 20 model fits, not a single fit.** The classifier keeps
every positive and draws a size-matched negative class, so one fit reports the probability of
one arbitrary draw; the draw alone moves test AUC by ~0.07 on these models. Section 2 reports
the spread and how often each construct's call flips.
`33h_construct_score_sweep.R` runs the sweep: `neg_seed` 1-20 for the classifiers, and
`split_seed` 1-20 for the regressions, which have no negative draw because they use all genes.

**Four models, all intrinsic (57 sequence-derived features).** The external block is 12
measurements made on endogenous genes (eIF3 CLIP, DAP5 sensitivity, published half-lives,
DHX29); a plasmid has none of them, and median-imputing would give all five constructs the
same values while shifting every score toward the average gene. So the intrinsic model is the
only version where every input is real.

| | hypoxia 1hr | normoxia 1+4hr |
|---|---|---|
| **classifier** | promoted vs negative controls, P(target) | same |
| **regression** | predicted TE log2FC on si3d, all genes | same |

**The features are computed from sequence**, because a plasmid has no annotation. That path is
re-implemented in `33b_`/`33c_`/`33d_` and **validated against the stored matrix** by
`33e_`/`33f_`/`33g_`: all 57 reproduce exactly on real transcripts. Sequences are parsed and
spliced by `33a_`.

**What this can and cannot say.** The models were trained on endogenous transcripts. These
constructs sit outside that population - a non-human CDS, vector UTRs, an unusual length
profile - and, more importantly, the adapted and anti-adapted variants were *designed* by
tuning codon usage, which is what several of the strongest features measure. A separation
between them is therefore close to arithmetic, not independent evidence. The informative
comparisons are the ones that were not built in: the size of the separation relative to real
transcripts, whether the ranking agrees across the two conditions and the two model types, and
whether the parent and its shuffled control (identical codon composition) come out together.

```{r libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse); library(here); library(ranger); library(treeshap)
})
O <- here("output", "translational_control_overview")
cache <- file.path(O, "plasmid_features.rds")

# Construct order, colours and short labels. Defined here because sections 2 and 3 both use them.
ord <- c("3d-adapted", "parent_bidir", "negative_control_3d", "3d-anti_adapted", "firefly")
# The Okabe-Ito orange and sky blue are reserved project-wide for eIF3d and eIF3e, and every
# construct here is an eIF3d experiment, so neither is used to label one construct. The parent
# and its shuffled control get black and grey rather than two near-identical greys.
# Firefly keeps the bluish green it carries in 62_, 68_ and cds_reporter_design/19_, so the
# normaliser is the same colour wherever it appears.
cols <- c("3d-adapted" = "#D55E00", "parent_bidir" = "black",
          "negative_control_3d" = "grey60", "3d-anti_adapted" = "#0072B2",
          "firefly" = "#009E73")
# All four NanoLuc variants are NanoLuc; "parent nano" names the unmodified one explicitly so a
# reader does not have to know that parent_bidir is the NanoLuc parent (33a_ asserts its CDS
# starts with the nanoluc_original designed sequence).
short <- c("3d-adapted" = "adapted", "parent_bidir" = "parent nano",
           "negative_control_3d" = "neg ctrl", "3d-anti_adapted" = "anti-adapted",
           "firefly" = "firefly")
stopifnot("every construct needs a colour and a short label" =
            all(ord %in% names(cols)) && all(ord %in% names(short)))

# How many individual features the per-feature SHAP figure shows.
TOP_N_FEAT <- 18
```

# 1. Features for the five constructs

```{r features}
pl <- read_csv(here("accessories", "transcribed_plasmids_parsed.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
FIREFLY <- "firefly"
NL4     <- c("parent_bidir", "negative_control_3d", "3d-adapted", "3d-anti_adapted")
nl4     <- pl %>% filter(construct %in% NL4)

stopifnot(
  "expected five constructs - run 33a_parse_plasmid_sequences.R" = nrow(pl) == 5,
  "the four NanoLuc constructs are not all present" = nrow(nl4) == 4,
  "firefly is missing" = FIREFLY %in% pl$construct,
  # Scoped to the NanoLuc four ON PURPOSE. Firefly has its own UTRs and is not a member of the
  # synonymous series; asserting one backbone across all five would fail on correct data.
  "the NanoLuc four are not one backbone" =
    n_distinct(nl4$utr5) == 1 && n_distinct(nl4$utr3) == 1,
  "the NanoLuc four no longer share one CDS length" = n_distinct(nl4$cds_nt) == 1,
  # The thing that makes firefly a different question, asserted rather than described.
  "firefly unexpectedly shares the NanoLuc backbone" =
    !pl$utr5[pl$construct == FIREFLY] %in% nl4$utr5)

if (params$recompute_features || !file.exists(cache)) {
  source(here("code", "translational_control_overview", "33b_sequence_features.R"))
  source(here("code", "translational_control_overview", "33c_structure_features.R"))
  source(here("code", "translational_control_overview", "33d_g4_features.R"))
  d  <- pl %>% transmute(id = construct, utr5, cds, utr3)
  sq <- seq_features(d)
  f  <- sq %>% left_join(structure_features(d), by = "id") %>%
               left_join(g4_features(d, sq), by = "id")
  saveRDS(f, cache)
} else {
  f <- readRDS(cache)
}

MODELS <- tribble(
  ~label,                  ~kind,         ~suffix,
  "hypoxia 1hr",           "classifier",  "eif33d_promotes_hypoxia_1hr_lfc0.5_tco_intrinsic_corrected_both_clipaggregate",
  "normoxia 1+4hr",        "classifier",  "eif33d_promotes_normoxia_1and4hr_lfc0.5_tco_intrinsic_corrected_both_clipaggregate",
  "hypoxia 1hr",           "regression",  "eif33d_promotes_hypoxia_1hr_lfc0.5_tcoreg_intrinsic_corrected_both_clipaggregate_yraw",
  "normoxia 1+4hr",        "regression",  "eif33d_promotes_normoxia_1and4hr_lfc0.5_tcoreg_intrinsic_corrected_both_clipaggregate_yraw")

md_of <- function(s, kind) readRDS(file.path(O, paste0(
  if (kind == "classifier") "rf_model_data_" else "rfreg_model_data_", s, ".rds")))
mdl_of <- function(s, kind) readRDS(file.path(O, paste0(
  if (kind == "classifier") "rf_classifier_" else "rfreg_model_", s, ".rds")))

FC <- md_of(MODELS$suffix[1], "classifier")$feature_cols
stopifnot("every model must use the same 57 features" =
            all(map_lgl(seq_len(nrow(MODELS)), ~ identical(md_of(MODELS$suffix[.x], MODELS$kind[.x])$feature_cols, FC))),
          "a feature is missing for the constructs" = all(FC %in% names(f)),
          "a construct feature is NA - the models would see an imputed value" =
            !anyNA(f[, FC]))
X <- as.data.frame(f[, FC]); rownames(X) <- f$id
cat("features:", length(FC), "| constructs:", nrow(X), "| no missing values\n")
```

## Which features can differ at all

**Two denominators, because there are two questions.** The NanoLuc four share a backbone and a
protein, so most features are identical by construction and only a handful of columns can
separate them - that handful is the honest denominator for the synonymous comparison, and
between the parent and its shuffled control only the position-dependent ones can move at all.
Firefly shares none of that, so for firefly nearly everything differs and the table says
little; what matters there is *which* differences the model acts on, which is section 3.

```{r what_varies}
n_varying <- function(d, who) {
  v <- d %>% dplyr::select(id, all_of(FC)) %>% pivot_longer(-id) %>%
    group_by(name) %>% summarise(n_distinct = n_distinct(round(value, 10)),
                                 spread = diff(range(value)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_distinct > 1) %>% arrange(desc(spread))
  cat(sprintf("%-22s %2d of %d features differ, %2d identical\n",
              who, nrow(v), length(FC), length(FC) - nrow(v)))
  v
}
varies_nl4 <- n_varying(f %>% filter(id %in% NL4), "NanoLuc four:")
varies_all <- n_varying(f,                          "all five:")

pn <- f %>% filter(id %in% c("parent_bidir", "negative_control_3d")) %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(FC)) %>% summarise(across(everything(), ~ diff(range(.x)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything()) %>% filter(value > 1e-10)
cat("\nparent vs negative control (identical codon composition):", nrow(pn), "features differ -",
    paste(pn$name, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Features that are CONSTANT across all five cannot explain any difference the models report.
# The vector supplies the start context, so the initiation family lands here - worth stating
# before any attribution, since "initiation strength" is then off the table by construction.
const5 <- setdiff(FC, varies_all$name)
cat("\nconstant across all five (cannot separate any construct):", length(const5), "\n  ",
    paste(const5, collapse = ", "), "\n")

cat("\nFeatures that vary within the NanoLuc synonymous series:\n")
print(as.data.frame(varies_nl4), digits = 4)
```

# 2. Predictions

A classifier probability is calibrated against a training set deliberately balanced 50/50
between eIF3d-promoted genes and negative controls, so 0.5 is **not** "a typical transcript".
It is reported next to the held-out distribution of each class, which is what makes it
readable. The regression predicts a TE log2 fold change directly and is placed against all
`r format(nrow(readRDS(file.path(O, "feature_matrix_tco.rds"))), big.mark = ",")` transcripts.

```{r predict}
ref_matrix <- readRDS(file.path(O, "feature_matrix_tco.rds"))

predict_one <- function(suffix, kind, label) {
  md <- md_of(suffix, kind); mdl <- mdl_of(suffix, kind)
  # Training medians impute the reference matrix exactly as the model was trained. Imputing with
  # a median leaves that median unchanged, so the saved (already imputed) training split carries
  # the same medians the model was fitted with.
  meds <- md$train %>% dplyr::select(all_of(FC)) %>% summarise(across(everything(), median, na.rm = TRUE))
  ref <- ref_matrix %>% dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, gene_id_clean, all_of(FC))
  for (cl in FC) ref[[cl]][is.na(ref[[cl]])] <- meds[[cl]]

  pr <- function(newdata) {
    p <- predict(mdl, data = as.data.frame(newdata))$predictions
    if (is.matrix(p)) p[, md$pos_label] else p
  }
  # EVERY gene in the matrix gets a prediction, whatever its role in fitting this model, so the
  # reference distribution is a MIXTURE of three populations with different meanings:
  #   trained on  - the forest fitted these rows, and predict() uses all 1000 trees including
  #                 the ones that saw them, so these predictions are overfit and pushed to the
  #                 extremes (measured below: sd ~1.5x the held-out sd in both model types)
  #   held out    - honest
  #   never seen  - honest. Only the CLASSIFIER has these: it fits the positives plus a
  #                 size-matched negative draw, so ~72% of the transcriptome was never in it.
  #                 The regression fits every gene, so 80% of ITS reference is training rows.
  # Percentiles against the mixture are therefore biased, which is why pct_honest exists.
  ref_pred <- pr(ref[, FC])
  status <- ifelse(ref$gene_id_clean %in% md$train$gene_id_clean, "trained on",
            ifelse(ref$gene_id_clean %in% md$test$gene_id_clean,  "held out", "never seen"))
  honest <- ref_pred[status != "trained on"]
  stopifnot("no honest reference genes - the split no longer carries gene ids" = length(honest) > 0)

  # Computed before the tibble: inside tibble(), `kind` would resolve to the column being
  # created rather than to the argument.
  is_pos <- if (kind == "classifier") md$test$eif3d_target == md$pos_label else md$test$y > 0.5
  tibble(label = label, kind = kind, suffix = suffix,
         construct = rownames(X), pred = pr(X[, FC]),
         ref_pred = list(ref_pred), ref_status = list(status), honest_pred = list(honest),
         test_pred = list(pr(md$test[, FC])),
         test_is_pos = list(is_pos))
}

preds <- pmap_dfr(list(MODELS$suffix, MODELS$kind, MODELS$label), predict_one) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(pct_transcriptome = 100 * mean(ref_pred < pred),
         # The reportable one: against genes this forest never fitted.
         pct_honest        = 100 * mean(honest_pred < pred),
         pct_heldout_pos   = 100 * mean(test_pred[test_is_pos] < pred)) %>%
  ungroup()

print(as.data.frame(preds %>% dplyr::select(kind, label, construct, pred, pct_transcriptome)), digits = 4)
```

```{r pred_table}
preds %>%
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%.3f (%.0f%%)", pred, pct_transcriptome)) %>%
  dplyr::select(construct, kind, label, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(kind, label), values_from = cell) %>%
  arrange(match(construct, ord)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print()
cat("\ncell = prediction (percentile among all transcripts under that model)\n")
```

## Across 20 fits - this is the reportable version

The table above is **one draw**. `33h_construct_score_sweep.R` refits each model 20 times,
varying only the thing that carries its noise - the negative draw for the classifiers
(`neg_seed`), the train/test split for the regressions (`split_seed`), which have no negative
draw because they use every gene. Within a seed all five constructs are scored by a model that
saw identical genes, so the comparison between constructs is paired even though the absolute
level moves.

**The call stability column is the one to read.** A classifier probability is calibrated against
a training set balanced 50/50, so 0.5 is the nominal cut; `frac_called` is the fraction of the
20 fits that put a construct above it. A construct at 10/20 has no call at all.

```{r sweep}
SW_P <- file.path(O, "construct_sweep_predictions.csv")
SW_S <- file.path(O, "construct_sweep_shap.csv")
stopifnot("run 33h_construct_score_sweep.R first" = file.exists(SW_P) && file.exists(SW_S))

sw <- read_csv(SW_P, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(construct = factor(construct, ord))
sw_shap <- read_csv(SW_S, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(construct = factor(construct, ord))

stopifnot(
  "the sweep does not cover all five constructs" = n_distinct(sw$construct) == 5,
  "the sweep features do not match the models' feature list" =
    setequal(unique(sw_shap$feature), FC))

n_seeds <- n_distinct(sw$seed)
cat(sprintf("%d seeds x %d constructs x %d model runs\n", n_seeds, n_distinct(sw$construct),
            n_distinct(paste(sw$kind, sw$label))))

sw_sum <- sw %>%
  group_by(kind, label, construct) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median = median(pred), sd = sd(pred),
            p05 = quantile(pred, 0.05), p95 = quantile(pred, 0.95),
            pct_tx = median(pct_transcriptome),
            frac_called = if (first(kind) == "classifier") mean(pred > 0.5) else NA_real_,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(kind, label, construct)

print(as.data.frame(sw_sum %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))))
```

```{r sweep_fig, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 6.5}
# Every fit as a point, the median as a bar. The draw-to-draw spread is the thing a single-fit
# figure hides, so it is drawn rather than summarised.
psw <- sw %>%
  mutate(panel = paste0(kind, " | ", label)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(pred, construct, colour = construct)) +
  geom_vline(data = tibble(panel = unique(paste0(sw$kind, " | ", sw$label))) %>%
               filter(str_starts(panel, "classifier")),
             aes(xintercept = 0.5), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.6,
             position = position_jitter(height = 0.12, width = 0, seed = 9)) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", shape = 124, size = 9, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = short) +
  labs(x = "prediction", y = NULL,
       title = sprintf("Five constructs, %d fits each", n_seeds),
       subtitle = "classifier: P(target), dashed line = the 50/50 nominal cut | regression: predicted si3d TE log2FC\nblack tick = median; each point is one fit, varying only the negative draw (classifier) or the split (regression)") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"))
print(psw)
ggsave(here("plots", "33_construct_sweep_predictions.pdf"), psw, width = 11, height = 6.5)
```

**Firefly against the series it normalises.** The paired difference is the readable quantity:
within each seed, firefly minus the parent NanoLuc. Pairing removes the draw-to-draw level
shift, which is several times larger than the difference being measured.

```{r sweep_paired}
paired <- sw %>%
  dplyr::select(kind, label, seed, construct, pred) %>%
  filter(construct %in% c("firefly", "parent_bidir")) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = construct, values_from = pred) %>%
  mutate(diff = firefly - parent_bidir)

print(as.data.frame(paired %>%
  group_by(kind, label) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median_diff = median(diff), sd_diff = sd(diff),
            n_firefly_higher = sum(diff > 0),
            p_wilcox = wilcox.test(firefly, parent_bidir, paired = TRUE)$p.value,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 3)))))

cat("\nFor scale, the draw-to-draw sd of the parent's own prediction:\n")
print(as.data.frame(sw %>% filter(construct == "parent_bidir") %>%
  group_by(kind, label) %>% summarise(sd_across_seeds = signif(sd(pred), 3), .groups = "drop")))
```

```{r fig_predictions, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 7.5}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggrepel))

# Two versions of the same panel, on purpose.
#   pooled - the original single-curve reading, with the PROVENANCE of the curve stated: which
#            genes it is made of and what role each played in fitting the model
#   split  - the same curve separated by that role, because an unlabelled mixture invites reading
#            a construct against a distribution that is 23% (classifier) or 80% (regression)
#            overfit training predictions
bg_all <- preds %>% dplyr::select(kind, label, ref_pred, ref_status) %>%
  distinct(kind, label, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  unnest(c(ref_pred, ref_status)) %>%
  mutate(panel = paste0(kind, " | ", label),
         ref_status = factor(ref_status, c("trained on", "held out", "never seen")))
status_lty <- c("trained on" = "dotted", "held out" = "solid", "never seen" = "dashed")

pt <- preds %>% mutate(panel = paste0(kind, " | ", label),
                       construct = factor(construct, ord), lab = short[as.character(construct)])

# Composition of the pooled curve, computed BEFORE the axis clipping so the numbers describe the
# whole reference set rather than the visible window.
comp <- bg_all %>% count(panel, ref_status) %>%
  group_by(panel) %>% mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n))) %>% ungroup()
comp_txt <- comp %>% group_by(panel) %>%
  summarise(txt = sprintf("%s = %s", panel[1],
                          paste(sprintf("%s %s (%d%%)", format(n, big.mark = ","),
                                        as.character(ref_status), pct), collapse = ", ")),
            .groups = "drop") %>% pull(txt) %>% paste(collapse = "\n")
cat("Composition of the reference distribution:\n", comp_txt, "\n", sep = "")

# The regression predictions occupy a narrow slice of a wide distribution, so an unzoomed axis
# stacks all five constructs on one tick. Each panel is clipped to the central 98% of its own
# reference distribution, widened if needed to hold every construct.
lims <- bg_all %>% group_by(panel) %>%
  summarise(lo = quantile(ref_pred, 0.01), hi = quantile(ref_pred, 0.99), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(pt %>% group_by(panel) %>% summarise(pmin = min(pred), pmax = max(pred), .groups = "drop"),
            by = "panel") %>%
  mutate(pad = 0.08 * (pmax(hi, pmax) - pmin(lo, pmin)),
         lo = pmin(lo, pmin) - pad, hi = pmax(hi, pmax) + pad)
bg <- bg_all %>% left_join(lims, by = "panel") %>% filter(ref_pred >= lo, ref_pred <= hi)

CAP_COMMON <- paste0(
  "Classifier: P(eIF3d-promoted), calibrated on a balanced training set, so 0.5 is not 'a typical transcript'. ",
  "Regression: predicted TE log2FC on si3d.")

build_fig <- function(split) {
  base <- ggplot(bg, aes(ref_pred))
  dens <- if (split)
    list(geom_density(aes(linetype = ref_status), colour = "grey35", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.55),
         scale_linetype_manual(values = status_lty, name = NULL))
  else
    list(geom_density(fill = "grey85", colour = "grey55", alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.4))

  base + dens +
    geom_vline(data = pt, aes(xintercept = pred, colour = construct), linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_text_repel(data = pt, aes(x = pred, y = 0, label = lab, colour = construct),
                    angle = 90, hjust = 0, size = 3.1, direction = "x", seed = 9,
                    box.padding = 0.25, min.segment.length = 0.1, segment.size = 0.3,
                    show.legend = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols, name = NULL, labels = short) +
    expand_limits(y = 0) +
    labs(x = "model prediction", y = "density",
         title = "Where the constructs fall against all transcripts",
         subtitle = if (split)
           sprintf("all %s transcripts scored by the same model, SPLIT BY ROLE IN FITTING; axes clipped to the central 98%%",
                   format(nrow(ref_matrix), big.mark = ","))
         else
           sprintf("all %s transcripts scored by the same model; axes clipped to the central 98%% of each distribution",
                   format(nrow(ref_matrix), big.mark = ",")),
         caption = if (split)
           paste0("Every gene is scored regardless of status. 'Trained on' predictions are overfit - predict() uses all trees, including those that saw the row -\n",
                  "so that curve is wider and should not be used to place a construct. Read against 'held out' and 'never seen'.\n",
                  "The classifier fits the positives plus a size-matched negative draw, so most of the transcriptome is never seen; the regression fits every gene.\n",
                  CAP_COMMON)
         else
           paste0("Where the predicted values come from: every transcript in feature_matrix_tco.rds is scored by the saved model, whatever its role in fitting it.\n",
                  comp_txt, "\n",
                  "'Trained on' predictions are overfit, so this pooled curve is wider than an honest one. See the split version for the same data separated by role.\n",
                  CAP_COMMON)) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 7.5, colour = "grey30"))
}

p_pooled <- build_fig(split = FALSE)
print(p_pooled)
ggsave(here("plots", "33_plasmid_predictions.pdf"), p_pooled, width = 12, height = 7.5)

p_split <- build_fig(split = TRUE)
print(p_split)
ggsave(here("plots", "33_plasmid_predictions_by_status.pdf"), p_split, width = 12, height = 7.5)
```

The four models use different scales, so percentile against the transcriptome is the one view
that puts them side by side.

```{r fig_percentile, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
pp <- preds %>% mutate(construct = factor(construct, rev(ord)),
                       panel = paste0(kind, " | ", label))
ppct <- ggplot(pp, aes(pct_transcriptome, construct, colour = construct)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, colour = "grey70", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 50, xend = pct_transcriptome, yend = construct), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f", pct_transcriptome)), vjust = -1.1, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = short) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100)) +
  labs(x = "percentile among all transcripts", y = NULL,
       title = "The same predictions on one comparable scale",
       subtitle = "dashed = the median transcript; higher = looks more like an eIF3d-dependent mRNA") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey92"))
print(ppct)
ggsave(here("plots", "33_plasmid_percentiles.pdf"), ppct, width = 9, height = 4.5)
```

# 3. Why: per-construct SHAP

SHAP is run on the **regression** models, where the forest is a regression forest and TreeSHAP
applies directly - no surrogate, so no fidelity apparatus is needed. (The classifier is a
probability forest, which `treeshap` cannot take; `03_shap.Rmd` handles that with a surrogate,
which is not worth importing for five sequences.) Values are additive, so a family's
contribution is the exact sum of its members'.

```{r shap, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7}
ann <- read_csv(file.path(O, "feature_annotation.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
shap_one <- function(suffix, label) {
  md <- md_of(suffix, "regression"); mdl <- mdl_of(suffix, "regression")
  uni <- ranger.unify(mdl, as.data.frame(md$train[, FC]))
  s <- treeshap(uni, X[, FC], verbose = FALSE)$shaps
  as_tibble(s) %>% mutate(construct = rownames(X), label = label, .before = 1)
}
shap <- map2_dfr(MODELS$suffix[MODELS$kind == "regression"],
                 MODELS$label[MODELS$kind == "regression"], shap_one)

fam <- shap %>% pivot_longer(all_of(FC), names_to = "feature", values_to = "shap") %>%
  left_join(ann %>% dplyr::select(feature, family), by = "feature") %>%
  group_by(label, construct, family) %>% summarise(shap = sum(shap), .groups = "drop")

pf <- fam %>%
  mutate(construct = factor(construct, ord),
         family = fct_reorder(family, abs(shap), .fun = max)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(shap, family, fill = construct)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ label) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "summed SHAP (predicted TE log2FC)", y = NULL,
       title = "What drives each construct's predicted TE change",
       subtitle = "Regression model, TreeSHAP; family sums are exact because SHAP is additive",
       caption = "Positive = pushes the predicted si3d TE log2FC up (more eIF3d-dependent).") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, colour = "grey30"))
print(pf)
ggsave(here("plots", "33_plasmid_shap_families.pdf"), pf, width = 11, height = 7)
print(as.data.frame(fam %>% pivot_wider(names_from = construct, values_from = shap)), digits = 3)
```

## Family attribution across 20 fits

The figure above is the default split. The sweep gives each family's contribution a spread, so
a family is only worth reading if its contribution is large next to that spread. Family sums are
**exact**, because SHAP is additive.

```{r shap_families_sweep, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7}
fam_sw <- sw_shap %>%
  left_join(ann %>% dplyr::select(feature, family), by = "feature") %>%
  group_by(label, seed, construct, family) %>%
  summarise(shap = sum(shap), .groups = "drop")

fam_med <- fam_sw %>%
  group_by(label, construct, family) %>%
  summarise(median = median(shap), p05 = quantile(shap, 0.05),
            p95 = quantile(shap, 0.95), .groups = "drop")

pfs <- fam_med %>%
  mutate(family = fct_reorder(family, abs(median), .fun = max)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(median, family, colour = construct)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = p05, xmax = p95),
                 position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ label) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols, name = NULL, labels = short) +
  labs(x = "summed SHAP (predicted si3d TE log2FC)", y = NULL,
       title = "What drives each construct's predicted TE change",
       subtitle = sprintf("Regression models, TreeSHAP. Point = median over %d fits, bar = 5-95%%. Family sums are exact.",
                          n_distinct(fam_sw$seed)),
       caption = "Positive = pushes the predicted si3d TE log2FC up (more eIF3d-dependent).") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, colour = "grey30"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"))
print(pfs)
ggsave(here("plots", "33_construct_sweep_shap_families.pdf"), pfs, width = 11, height = 7)
```

## Per-feature, ordered by the hypoxia regression model's own importance

The family figure sums within a block, which is the right way to resolve credit between
correlated columns but hides which member moves. This is the same decomposition drawn per
**feature**, for the top `r TOP_N_FEAT` features of the **hypoxia regression** model ranked by
that model's impurity importance, and the same features are shown in both panels so the two
conditions are directly comparable.

**Bars of equal length across all five constructs mean the feature is constant.** SHAP is
measured against the training baseline, not against the other constructs, so a feature every
construct shares still carries a large contribution - it just cannot explain any difference
between them. The Kozak columns are the clearest case.

```{r shap_features_fig, fig.width = 12, fig.height = 8.5}
imp_hyp <- read_csv(
  file.path(O, paste0("rfreg_importance_",
                      MODELS$suffix[MODELS$kind == "regression" & MODELS$label == "hypoxia 1hr"],
                      ".csv")), show_col_types = FALSE)
stopifnot("the hypoxia regression importance file does not carry the model's features" =
            all(FC %in% imp_hyp$feature))

top_feats <- imp_hyp %>% arrange(desc(importance)) %>% slice_head(n = TOP_N_FEAT) %>% pull(feature)

# Constant features are marked on the axis rather than dropped: that they rank highly and still
# explain nothing between constructs is the point.
const_feats <- setdiff(FC, varies_all$name)

# Axis labels: shorten the RNAplfold prefix, which is long enough to be clipped, and mark any
# feature that is constant across the five constructs.
pretty_feat <- function(x) sub("^tco_struct_accessibility_", "struct_", x)
lab_of <- setNames(
  paste0(pretty_feat(top_feats), ifelse(top_feats %in% const_feats, "  (constant)", "")),
  top_feats)
stopifnot("two features collapsed to the same axis label" = !any(duplicated(lab_of)))

# top_feats is in descending importance. A discrete ggplot axis places level 1 at the BOTTOM, so
# the levels run least-important first and the biggest driver ends up at the TOP.
feat_plot <- sw_shap %>%
  filter(feature %in% top_feats) %>%
  group_by(label, construct, feature) %>%
  summarise(median = median(shap), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(flab = factor(lab_of[as.character(feature)], levels = rev(unname(lab_of))))

pff <- ggplot(feat_plot, aes(median, flab, fill = construct)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.78), width = 0.72) +
  facet_wrap(~ label) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols, name = NULL, labels = short) +
  labs(x = "median SHAP over 20 fits (predicted si3d TE log2FC)", y = NULL,
       title = "What drives each construct's predicted TE change, per feature",
       subtitle = sprintf("Top %d features of the HYPOXIA regression model by its own importance, same features in both panels",
                          TOP_N_FEAT),
       caption = paste0("Positive = pushes the predicted si3d TE log2FC up (more eIF3d-dependent).\n",
                        "Equal bars across all five = a constant feature: it contributes, but explains no difference between constructs.")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, colour = "grey30"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"))
print(pff)
ggsave(here("plots", "33_construct_sweep_shap_features.pdf"), pff, width = 12, height = 8.5)

cat("\nRank in the hypoxia regression model, and whether the feature can separate constructs:\n")
print(as.data.frame(imp_hyp %>% arrange(desc(importance)) %>% slice_head(n = TOP_N_FEAT) %>%
  transmute(rank = row_number(), feature, importance = round(importance, 1),
            separates = ifelse(feature %in% const_feats, "NO - constant across all five", "yes"))))
```

## Top per-feature drivers

Family sums hide which member is doing the work, which matters most for firefly: its gc and
length families move for several reasons at once. These are the individual features with the
largest median |SHAP| per construct, with the sign.

```{r shap_features_sweep}
feat_med <- sw_shap %>%
  group_by(label, construct, feature) %>%
  summarise(median = median(shap), p05 = quantile(shap, 0.05),
            p95 = quantile(shap, 0.95),
            # A driver whose sign is not stable across fits is not a driver.
            frac_same_sign = max(mean(shap > 0), mean(shap < 0)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(ann %>% dplyr::select(feature, family), by = "feature")

top_drivers <- feat_med %>%
  group_by(label, construct) %>%
  slice_max(abs(median), n = 8, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  arrange(label, construct, desc(abs(median))) %>%
  ungroup()

print(as.data.frame(top_drivers %>%
  dplyr::select(label, construct, feature, family, median, p05, p95, frac_same_sign) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))))

write_csv(feat_med, file.path(O, "construct_sweep_shap_features.csv"))
write_csv(fam_med,  file.path(O, "construct_sweep_shap_families.csv"))
write_csv(sw_sum,   file.path(O, "construct_sweep_summary.csv"))
cat("\nwrote construct_sweep_shap_features.csv, construct_sweep_shap_families.csv, construct_sweep_summary.csv\n")
```
